newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB cuts 1996/97 pool prices by A$2.00/tonne.
newsitem.headline: AWB cuts 1996/97 pool prices by A$2.00/tonne.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Monday it had reduced its 1996/97 pool prices by A$2.00 a tonne and its 1997/98 estimate by A$10.00 a tonne.
The prices were reduced in response to recent falls in international wheat prices, AWB general manager merchandising Ron Storey said.
The cuts take the 1996/97 pool price of Australian Standard White (ASW) to A$198.00 a tonne and the estimate for 1997/98 to a range of A$180.00-A$190.00 a tonne.
The international market was focused on U.S. supply factors including the current harvest which at present was coming in with favourable reports on quality and yield, he said.

The adjustment in the 1997/98 pool estimates reflected this but also took into consideration uncertainty associated with Australia's 1997/98 crop size and the uncertain impact El Nino would have on the growing season, he said.
"While plantings are in a reasonable condition overall, the prospect of below average rainfall in the next six months is certainly a concern," he said.
As a result of El Nino, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) will be putting out a special crop report in July, ahead of the normal September forecast, AWB said.
The new pool price figures represented a balance between the fall in international demand and the current ABARE wheat crop forecast for 1997/98 of 16.25 million tonnes, Storey said.
Pool prices for 1996/97 wheat at June 23
The next pool price update will be on July 7.
